subject: Request: Tight routing + no-fallback exemption for Clearpath pilot
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria@clearpath.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@clearpath.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot needs: geo-locked routing + no-fallback

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday — the team is excited. Before we move to an internal pilot, our security and compliance folks have a firm requirement: all inference requests for our tenant must be pinned to the us-east region and must not fall back to any other model variant or region.

We understand Redwood has fallbacks to preserve availability; Clearpath is asking for a tight routing exception (geo-lock + no-fallback) for the 3-month pilot. Attached is a short requirements doc and an SLA exception request from procurement.

Specific asks: 
- Strictly route to us-east and only to model variant `clearpath-1.0` (we will pin the model id).
- If capacity isn't available, fail the request rather than route elsewhere.
- Audit logs for each request showing model_id, host, and decisioning.

Can you outline what is feasible and what risks we should expect? Procurement also wants to understand whether this affects uptime SLAs or pricing.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Product Integrations
Clearpath Analytics

---
Attachments: Clearpath_Routing_Requirements.pdf, SLA-exception-request.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria@clearpath.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Pilot needs: geo-locked routing + no-fallback

Marissa / Karthik / Markus — looping you in. Clearpath (potential pilot) is requesting a strict geo-lock to us-east and a no-fallback behavior for the duration of a 3-month pilot. They will pin to model `clearpath-1.0`. Their procurement asked for an SLA exception.

Quick notes / questions to triage:
- Marissa (Product): is there a product/contract precedent for a hard no-fallback? What are the UX/monitoring implications?
- Karthik (Infra/Serving): do we have a safe way to configure a per-tenant routing policy that returns 5xx when capacity is insufficient (instead of routing to another region/model)?
- Markus (Security/Privacy): any residual compliance concerns if we force single-region and disable fallback? Audit logging looks required.

I'd like a short internal decision paper by EOD Monday (22nd) so we can respond with options and risk/impact. If any of you prefer a quick sync, I can set up 30 min.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment(s): none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria@clearpath.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Pilot needs: geo-locked routing + no-fallback

Thanks Rishi — quick thoughts from product side.

Summary: technically possible with tradeoffs. Options to offer Clearpath (short, clear bullets for reply):

1) Strict pin + fail-on-capacity (what they asked): implement as tenant-level routing policy. Pros: meets compliance. Cons: higher perceived downtime for them, operational burden on capacity planning. Requires a signed SLA exception.

2) Strict pin + queued retries within region (soft improvement): keep all requests in-region and queue briefly (200–500ms windows) before failing. Better UX, still meets residency.

3) Primary-region with audited emergency fallback (automated but logged and requires exec approval): fallback allowed only if explicit emergency conditions met; we'd surface and require Clearpath acknowledgement.

Requirements for any option:
- Per-request audit trail with model_id, host_id, region, routing_decision, and timestamp (we can capture).
- Config UI + API flag to opt into the policy at tenant-level; we need a small schema change (1–2 sprints).

Impact estimates:
- Infra engineering (Karthik): 2–3 engineer-weeks for config + fail-path + audit plumbing.
- Product/Console: 1 sprint for opt-in toggle + UX.
- Support: runbook and alerting (1 week).

I recommend offering option 2 to start (queue then fail) and keep option 1 as available for customers who explicitly accept the availability risk.

Marissa Cole
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria@clearpath.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 14:34:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Pilot needs: geo-locked routing + no-fallback

Folks — short infra commitment and next steps (operational / tickets).

Feasibility: confirmed. We can gate per-tenant routing and return a 5xx on capacity shortfall, or implement a short regional queue. Implementation plan:
- Create tenant-routing policy object (db schema change) that includes region list, allowed_model_ids, and fallback_behavior enum (FAIL | QUEUE | ALLOW_EMERGENCY). (INF-9123)
- Add enforcement in the routing layer: when a request arrives, check policy; if region matches and model available, proceed; if not available: QUEUE -> short delay then fail; FAIL -> return 503 with structured error; ALLOW_EMERGENCY -> call exec approval hook.
- Audit trail: new log event (route.decide) with model_id, host, region, decision, request_id (we'll store to existing logs/ELK).

Estimate: 3 engineer-weeks (two engineers) to ship a minimal safe implementation (QUEUE+FAIL), plus 1 week for audit and alerting. We can scope out ALLOW_EMERGENCY in a follow-up.

Operational asks for Clearpath pilot:
- Signed acknowledgement of potential for increased 5xx/failed requests and how Redwood will notify.
- Lead contact for capacity runbook and escalation.

If you want, I can spin up the initial Jira (INF-9123) and a short runbook draft and share with Maria.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---
Action items:
- Rishi: confirm which option Clearpath prefers (FAIL or QUEUE).
- Marissa: prepare short decision memo and pricing uplift for SLA exception.
- Karthik: create INF ticket and runbook draft.

Cc: Maria — we'll include the runbook and ticket once created.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 18:34:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Pilot needs: geo-locked routing + no-fallback

Maria — thanks for the quick turnaround. We can support this pilot but want to be explicit about tradeoffs. Options we can offer:

A) Queue-then-fail (recommended): Redwood will enforce tenant-level geo-lock to us-east, keep requests within-region, perform short queued retries (200–500ms), and then fail with 503 if capacity is still unavailable. We will provide per-request audit logs and a pilot runbook. Implementation ETA: ~3 weeks to ship minimal infra and runbook.

B) Hard-fail (no-fallback, immediate 503): enforce geo-lock and return 503 immediately on capacity shortfall. Implementation ETA: ~2 weeks but requires a signed SLA exception acknowledging availability risk.

C) Emergency fallback with approval: allow fallback only under customer-approved emergency conditions; timeline depends on exec hooks (TBD).

Please confirm if Clearpath wants Option A (preferred by Product/Infra) or Option B (requires procurement approval). Once you confirm, we'll create the INF-9123 ticket and share the runbook + HubSpot update with procurement.

Appreciate the clear requirements — we'll proceed once you pick an option.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
